Looking at the pattern, F0 and F1 are both signaling 0.1550. F2 is being vague ("market realities"). 

In a second-price auction, I want to win with the lowest bid and get paid the second-lowest. If F0 and F1 are at 0.1550 and I bid just below (e.g., 0.1499), I win but get paid the second-lowest which would be 0.1499 (if others also bid low) or higher.

If I bid 0.1499 and F0/F1 actually bid 0.1550, I win and get paid 0.1550 - excellent margin.

If F2 also bids low (say 0.1499), we tie and clearing is 0.1499 - still above my cost of capital of 0.1117.

The dominant strategy in second-price auctions is to bid my true value (cost of capital), but since I must stay above 0.1117 to not lose money, bidding aggressively low captures the win and gets paid the second price. If others coordinate at 0.1550, I profit greatly by undercutting.
